top_signal.title: Should I setup a LLC and get E&O insurance before doing 1099 contract work?
top_signal.summary: Hi   I'm applying for jobs in the tech/analytics sector. On certain job boards, I see positions that are labeled as "contract". I'm also in a startup community where some founders would post 1099 work.    This got my thinking, should I setup a LLC and get E&O insurance before taking on such jobs? I've been working as a W2 employee all my life but am trying to get more contract work for flexibility.   The way I understand, when you work as a W2 employee, you are typically not liable for mistakes that cause damage for the employer (you might be fired though). However, working as a contractor provides no such protection and therefore your personal assets might be at risk. I hope to understand more about this and how do consulant/freelancers typically protect themselves and what do you recommend for my situation.    I also heard it's possible to state in the contract that the maximum liability would be limited to a certain dollar amount. How often is this clause used?   Just want to know what's the "typical" ways freelancers handle this. I'm new to this. But it'd be pretty weird if I apply to a contract job on a job board and then mention "hey, I need to setup an LLC first before I can start".   Thanks       submitted by     /u/EyeTechnical7643       [link]       [comments]
